core.title: Advance plan-session stages only through their exit gates
core.given: A plan session (a gated decomposition session started by the stack's plan command) runs the stages Intent -> Attach -> Compose -> Ratify, then author -> verify -> modify.
core.when: The planner is about to move the session to the next stage.
core.then: Advance only when the current stage's exit state holds: Intent = the main job is kept; Attach = the sources and the state of the plan-artifact root are captured; Compose = the candidate decomposition is convention-shaped; Ratify = the operator has locked the decomposition.
prefer: Talk freely within a stage; the gate defines only the exit state, not a script.
Backtrack when useful: a pivot may reopen an earlier stage.
Name stages by what the operator is deciding, not by what the tool is doing.
avoid: Authoring anything before the Ratify gate; Ratify is the conversational-to-deterministic boundary, enforced by the companion confirm-before-author rule.
Treating the session stages and the job steps of the plan artifact as one system or one vocabulary; job steps are owned by the job-steps convention.
Advancing a stage when its exit state does not hold.
core.why: Gating on exit state keeps the decomposition dialogue flexible while guaranteeing nothing deterministic is authored until the operator has ratified a convention-shaped decomposition.
evidence: The session record shows, for each forward stage transition, that the exit state held: main job kept, sources and plan-artifact-root state captured, convention-shaped candidate decomposition, operator lock.
No authored plan artifact predates the operator's Ratify lock.
Reopening an earlier stage after a pivot is permitted and is not counted as a violation; it is optional, not required.
verification: Scope: the fixed stage order Intent -> Attach -> Compose -> Ratify, then author -> verify -> modify; a forward stage transition is compliant only when the exited stage's exit state held.

Gates are exit states, not scripts: free dialogue within a stage and backtracking (a pivot reopening an earlier stage) are permitted behavior and never violations; the ratification gate is the conversational-to-deterministic boundary, and nothing deterministic may be authored before it.
The ratification gate's authoring prohibition is owned by a companion confirm-before-author rule, not by a rule named after the stage; do not expect a rule named after Ratify.
Session-stage names and the plan artifact's job-step names are separate vocabularies owned by different conventions; a check must not match one vocabulary against the other.

Knowing the current stage and whether its exit state holds requires a session-state observer, which this rule does not itself provide; only the advancement obligation is scoped to stage transitions, so within-stage dialogue is not judged as advancement.

fires: Any point in a plan session, including free dialogue within a stage (stage naming and vocabulary separation still apply).
A plan session is about to move from Intent to Attach, Attach to Compose, Compose to Ratify, or Ratify to authoring.
The planner is about to author plan artifacts before the operator has locked the decomposition.
The operator pivots mid-session and the planner considers returning to an earlier stage.
The planner names or describes session stages, or refers to the plan artifact's job steps, during the session.
doesNotFire: Authoring or reviewing the plan artifact's job steps under the job-steps convention outside any plan session.
Work that is not part of a plan decomposition session.

profileRequirements.meaning: Root of plan artifacts; the Attach exit state requires the sources and the state of this root to be captured (core then and evidence[0]).

The stack's local name for the plan artifact, needed to keep the session-stage vocabulary separate from the plan artifact's job-step vocabulary (activation.facts[2], avoid[1], verifier_detail[3], activation fires/doesNotFire).
The command that starts a gated plan session; it is the operation value of activation.facts[0] and the session named in given, fires and doesNotFire.

bunOnly.reason: Corpus id of the companion rule that enforces the ratification gate; other realizations may name that rule differently, so the core refers to it by concept ('the companion confirm-before-author rule').

Corpus id of the convention that owns the plan artifact's job steps; the core names that convention by role ('the job-steps convention'), not by id. The same id also appears in the activation.facts[2] note and in doesNotFire.

bunOnly.text: Term aliases: session_stages = the four gates with exit states; gate_not_script = dynamic conversation within a stage, gate defines only exit state, a pivot may reopen an earlier stage; ratify_before_author = Ratify is the conversational->deterministic boundary, nothing authored before it.
bunOnly.reason: The alias map binds this realization's source term ids to the rule text; the neutral semantics those terms name are already carried in core then, prefer[0], prefer[1], avoid[0] and verification.

bunOnly.text: The Ratify stage's rule is named planner.plan.confirm-before-author (stage is Ratify, rule is confirm-before-author)
bunOnly.reason: Names a corpus rule id; the core keeps only the generic guidance that a companion confirm-before-author rule owns the gate's prohibition.
Corpus id of the job-steps convention; the core describes the ownership generically.

neutralityNotes: This is a process (session-lifecycle) rule, so almost all of it is already stack-neutral; the stage names Intent/Attach/Compose/Ratify and author/verify/modify are the convention's own process vocabulary and stay in the core. What is not neutral: (1) the plan command 'atdd plan', carried by the proposed key tooling.commands#plan_command; (2) the plan root 'plan/', carried by roots.plan; (3) the plan artifact's local name 'DESIRED OUTCOME', carried by roles.plan_artifact.name; (4) corpus ids of companion conventions and rules ('steps.convention', 'planner.plan.confirm-before-author') and the source term aliases (session_stages, gate_not_script, ratify_before_author), which are bunOnly with the core referring to them by concept. The same corpus ids also appear inside activation.fires/doesNotFire prose, where the core uses the generic phrasing and the bunOnly entries supply the exact ids. activation.facts[2]'s core value list omits 'DESIRED OUTCOME' because it is profile-supplied; core values plus the profile name equal the Bun set exactly.
